questiontext.text: In which order are the vertices computed in tree DP?

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. The value of a parent is built from its children, so the children must be ready first (post-order).

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

questiontext.text:
What does this program print?

main.cpp
vector<vector<int>> adj = {{}, {2, 3}, {1, 4}, {1}, {2}};
int val[5] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};
vector<long long> sum(5, 0);
function<void(int, int)> dfs = [&](int v, int p) {
    sum[v] = val[v];
    for (int u : adj[v]) {
        if (u != p) {
            dfs(u, v);
            sum[v] += sum[u];
        }
    }
};
dfs(1, 0);
cout << sum[2] << endl;

Assume the needed #include lines and using namespace std; are already written.

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. Vertex 2 has the value 2 and one child, vertex 4 with value 4. So sum[2] = 2 + 4 = 6.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

questiontext.text: What is the value of sum[v] for a leaf?

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. A leaf has no children to add, so its subtree contains only itself.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

answer.text: The value of the leaf itself

questiontext.text:
What does this program print?

main.cpp
vector<vector<int>> adj = {{}, {2}, {1, 3}, {2}};
vector<int> take(4, 1), skip(4, 0);
function<void(int, int)> dfs = [&](int v, int p) {
    for (int u : adj[v]) {
        if (u != p) {
            dfs(u, v);
            take[v] += skip[u];
            skip[v] += max(take[u], skip[u]);
        }
    }
};
dfs(1, 0);
cout << max(take[1], skip[1]) << endl;

Assume the needed #include lines and using namespace std; are already written.

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. The tree is the path 1-2-3. We can take vertices 1 and 3 (not adjacent), so the largest independent set has size 2.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

questiontext.text: In the independent set problem, what does take[v] mean?

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. It is the best size when we are forced to take v; skip[v] is the best when we avoid it.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

answer.text: The best set in the subtree of v that includes v

questiontext.text:
What does this program print?

main.cpp
vector<vector<int>> adj = {{}, {2, 3}, {1}, {1, 4}, {3, 5}, {4}};
vector<int> down(6, 0);
int diameter = 0;
function<void(int, int)> dfs = [&](int v, int p) {
    int best1 = 0, best2 = 0;
    for (int u : adj[v]) {
        if (u != p) {
            dfs(u, v);
            int d = down[u] + 1;
            if (d > best1) {
                best2 = best1;
                best1 = d;
            } else if (d > best2) {
                best2 = d;
            }
        }
    }
    down[v] = best1;
    diameter = max(diameter, best1 + best2);
};
dfs(1, 0);
cout << down[1] << " " << down[3] << endl;

Assume the needed #include lines and using namespace std; are already written.

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. From vertex 3 the longest downward path goes 3-4-5, which is 2 edges. From the root the path 1-3-4-5 has 3 edges.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

questiontext.text:
Match each term with its meaning.

Drag each description onto the item it belongs to.

State  →  [[1]]

Transition  →  [[2]]

Base case  →  [[3]]

Post-order  →  [[4]]

Independent set  →  [[5]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. These are the basic words of tree DP.

The correct answer:

  • State → What we define for the subtree of a vertex
  • Transition → The rule that builds a state from the children
  • Base case → The value for a leaf
  • Post-order → Children are handled before the parent
  • Independent set → Vertices with no edge between any two

questiontext.text:
Does the problem need two states (take and skip)?

Drag the correct label next to every item.

Largest independent set  →  [[1]]

Invite guests but never an employee together with their direct boss  →  [[1]]

Choose vertices so that no two are adjacent  →  [[1]]

Subtree sum  →  [[2]]

Size of each subtree  →  [[2]]

Longest downward path  →  [[2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. When choosing a vertex restricts its neighbors we must remember whether it was chosen. Sums, sizes and longest paths do not depend on such a choice.

The correct answer:

Two states needed: Largest independent set, Invite guests but never an employee together with their direct boss, Choose vertices so that no two are adjacent
One state is enough: Subtree sum, Size of each subtree, Longest downward path

questiontext.text:
Match each line with its job.

Drag each description onto the item it belongs to.

dfs(u, v);  →  [[1]]

sum[v] += sum[u];  →  [[2]]

take[v] += skip[u];  →  [[3]]

skip[v] += max(take[u], skip[u]);  →  [[4]]

diameter = max(diameter, best1 + best2);  →  [[5]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. These lines appear in the tree DP programs of the lesson.

The correct answer:

  • dfs(u, v); → Solves the child first
  • sum[v] += sum[u]; → Adds a child subtree to its parent
  • take[v] += skip[u]; → Taking v forbids taking the child
  • skip[v] += max(take[u], skip[u]); → Skipping v leaves the child free
  • diameter = max(diameter, best1 + best2); → Updates the longest path through v

questiontext.text:
Which statements about tree DP are true?

Drag the correct label next to every item.

Children are computed before the parent  →  [[1]]

It runs in O(n)  →  [[1]]

Leaves need a base case  →  [[1]]

The parent is computed first  →  [[2]]

Every vertex needs a visited array  →  [[2]]

The answer is always at a leaf  →  [[2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. Tree DP is a post-order computation that runs in linear time, starts from the base case at the leaves, and reads the answer at the root. It does not need a visited array.

The correct answer:

True: Children are computed before the parent, It runs in O(n), Leaves need a base case
False: The parent is computed first, Every vertex needs a visited array, The answer is always at a leaf
